# MediterraneApp

> Spring Boot 4.1 / Java 17 REST API for recipes, ingredients, and preparation steps.
> Legacy portfolio project (2020): builds, has a test suite and CI, but no
> authentication or maintained deployment. License: GPL-3.0.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): canonical guide for AI coding agents.
- [README.md](README.md): human-facing overview and quick start.
- [docs/API.md](docs/API.md): endpoints, payloads, status codes, and quirks.
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): layers, request flow, persistence model.
- [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md): prioritized defects and suggested fixes.
- [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md): local PostgreSQL, Docker, legacy Heroku.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): contribution workflow.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): private reporting and credential rotation.

## Project facts

- Package: `com.ges.mediterraneapp`.
- Entry point: `MediterraneappApplication`.
- Controller: `RecipeController`, base path `/recipe`.
- Services: `RecipeService`, `IngredientService`.
- Mappers: `RecipeMapper`, `IngredientMapper` (hand-written, no MapStruct).
- Entities: `Recipe`, `Ingredient`.
- Repositories: `RecipeRepository`, `IngredientRepository`, plus unused
  `StepRepository`.
- Build and test: `./mvnw -B verify`. Tests run on H2 in PostgreSQL mode, so no
  database is required. CI runs the same command on JDK 17.
- Configuration: `src/main/resources/application.yml`; override the datasource with
  `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`,
  `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD`.

## API summary

- `GET /recipe/status` -> HTTP 200 body `"I_AM_A_TEAPOT"`.
- `GET /recipe` -> all recipes.
- `GET /recipe/{uuid}` -> one recipe, 500 if absent.
- `POST /recipe` -> create or update by `name`, 201.
- `POST /recipe/bulk` -> batch create/update, HTTP 200 body `"CREATED"`.
- `PUT /recipe/{uuid}` -> update; send the same UUID in the body.
- `DELETE /recipe/{uuid}` -> delete, HTTP 200 body `"OK"`.

## Safety

- The repository is public. Do not add secrets, real `.env` files, Jasypt keys, or
  database credentials.
- The checked-in database host, username, and `ENC(...)` password are historical and
  must be treated as compromised. Rotate them before use.
- Do not run tests or the application against the remote database.
- See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) before reporting or fixing a credential leak.
